question.problem: Find where the tangent to the curve $y={x}^{4}-5$ at the point $(-1,-4)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{4}-5.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{4}-5)=4{x}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is

$$
m={f}^{′}(-1)=4(-1)^{3}=-4.
$$

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-4) & =-4(x+1) \\ y & =-4x-4-4 \\ y & =-4x-8.\end{aligned}
$$

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $y=0$ and solve:

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =-4x-8 \\ x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(-2,0).$
